description:
## Outcome

A trusted first-party built-in extension registers the coding pack, and one workspace service enforces root, canonical path, symlink, ignore, tool replacement, and project-instruction discovery rules.

## Why now

The default tools need a common security and replacement base. Building individual file or shell tools first would duplicate path and policy logic.

## Current state

`Jido.Cli.DefaultAgent` has instructions but no tools. No read, search, write, edit, shell, Git, ignore, or project instruction module exists. The built-in extension host and execution environment from earlier phases provide the correct seams.

## Ownership and boundary

This is a `jidoka` built-in extension change. The coding pack is enabled by trusted host configuration and can be disabled or replaced. Jidoka owns tool contracts and workspace enforcement. The CLI later chooses the default and presents context. Agent data cannot choose a raw root.

## Detailed implementation

1. Add a first-party coding-pack registration with stable pack and tool IDs. Do not activate it in the kernel by default.
2. Add a trusted workspace descriptor with canonical root, read/write classes, ignore sources, instruction filenames, byte/result limits, and execution profile reference.
3. Add one path resolver that rejects root escapes, unsafe symlink traversal, special files, and invalid encodings as appropriate.
4. Add deterministic ignore-rule evaluation for `.gitignore`-style files plus trusted exclusions. Define nested precedence and default secret/generated exclusions.
5. Add bounded project-instruction discovery with deterministic nearest-to-root order and provenance. Discovery returns data only.
6. Define host-only disable/replace rules for each default tool ID and collision checks.
7. Expose policy resource summaries for later tools.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The coding pack can be registered, disabled, or replaced without a kernel change.
- [ ] Workspace roots come only from trusted host configuration.
- [ ] Canonical paths cannot escape by `..`, absolute path, symlink, or case trick on supported systems.
- [ ] Ignore decisions and instruction order are deterministic and explainable.
- [ ] Ignored secret files cannot be selected by later tools.
- [ ] No file or command executes in this foundation story.

## Test plan

- Success: temp workspace, nested ignore files, instruction discovery, and tool replacement.
- Invalid input: missing root, file root, path escape, symlink escape, bad pattern, duplicate tool ID, and oversized instruction.
- Runtime failure: filesystem stat/read failure returns typed workspace error.
- Boundary and security: ignored `.env`, `.git`, generated tree, special file, and untrusted raw root request.
- Deterministic capability: inject filesystem/path case behavior and fixed workspace data where practical.
- JSONL and exit status: workspace and instruction projections are portable; no direct output.

## Documentation

Add a coding-pack architecture guide with tool IDs, trusted workspace settings, ignore precedence, instruction order, and disable/replace examples.

## Non-goals

Do not implement file contents, edits, shell, Git, `@file`, or TUI review. Do not activate tools unconditionally.

## Dependencies

Blocking issues:

- `jido_cli-tqg.4.4` — Add the built-in Jidoka extension host
- `jido_cli-tqg.3.4` — Implement the execution-environment lifecycle manager

Features unlocked by this story:

- Read and search tools
- Write and edit tools
- Constrained shell and Git tools

## Commit plan

Create exactly one focused `jidoka` commit. Use a message such as `feat(jidoka): define the removable coding pack (jido_cli-tqg.5.1)`. Do not include another backlog feature.

## Verification commands

```sh
cd /Users/mhostetler/Source/Jido/proj_jido_cli/jidoka
mix test test/jidoka/coding_pack/workspace_test.exs test/jidoka/coding_pack/registration_test.exs
mix quality
mix test
mix docs
```
title: Define the removable coding pack and workspace boundary
